headline: Record quarter caps a record year on broad recovery

kpis.label: Net income attributable to common shareholders

summary_short: Parker Hannifin's fiscal 2026 fourth quarter sales rose 9.8% y/y to a record $5.76B (8.0% organic), with GAAP diluted EPS up 19% to $8.54 and Adjusted Diluted EPS up 21% to a record $9.27; the company issued initial FY2027 guidance of $30.00-$31.00 GAAP EPS.
summary_long: Sales grew 9.8% y/y (8.0% organic) to a record $5.76B, led by Aerospace Systems (+13.4% reported, record backlog) and broad-based industrial growth including 16% organic growth in Asia Pacific. Segment operating margin rose 260bps to 26.5%; Adjusted margin rose 110bps to 28.0%, aided by an $84M one-off IEEPA tariff-refund benefit recognized in cost of sales. Net income rose 18% to $1,091M; GAAP diluted EPS rose 19% to $8.54, Adjusted Diluted EPS rose 21% to a record $9.27. Full-year operating cash flow hit a record $4.36B (20.3% of sales); shareholders' equity grew to $15.4B from $13.7B. Parker issued initial FY2027 guidance of 5.5%-8.5% sales growth and $30.00-$31.00 GAAP EPS ($34.25-$35.25 adjusted), and raised its FY2031 adjusted segment-margin target 300bps to 30%.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based: Aerospace Systems sales rose 13.4% (record backlog, double-digit growth in all market segments); Diversified Industrial International grew 9.5%, led by 16% organic growth in Asia Pacific; North America grew 7.0% as the industrial recovery broadened.
Tracks net income growth (+18%) on higher segment operating income and a lower diluted share count from continued buybacks; not separately decomposed for basic vs diluted in the release.
Net income rose 18% to $1,091M while diluted shares outstanding fell to 127.8M from 129.0M on continued buybacks, together lifting diluted EPS growth above net-income growth.

Adjusted EPS ($9.27) exceeds GAAP EPS ($8.54) mainly because amortization of acquired intangibles ($1.16/share) is added back, outweighing the removal of the $0.65/share one-off tariff-refund benefit included in GAAP results.
Margin expansion reflects sales growth outpacing cost growth plus the $84M tariff-refund reduction to cost of sales; the adjusted margin measure strips that one-off out and still rose 110bps.
Rose 110bps to 28.0% even after excluding the tariff-refund benefit, driven by record adjusted margins in both Diversified Industrial International and Aerospace Systems this quarter.

drivers.metric: Net income attributable to common shareholders
drivers.explanation: Tracks 9.8% sales growth and 260bps of GAAP segment-margin expansion (including the $84M tariff-refund benefit), partly offset by a higher effective tax rate (18.5% vs 13.8% a year ago).
Company highlights this as a full-year record (20.3% of sales) without further quantified decomposition in the release.
Reflects the board's 11% annualized dividend increase during fiscal 2026, marking a 70th consecutive year of increases; not tied to this quarter's earnings specifically.
Company attributes the record $12.8B backlog to increases across all three segments, with orders up 19% company-wide in the quarter (24% International, 18% Aerospace, 16% North America).

Guidance excludes the pending Filtration Group and CIRCOR aerospace-defense acquisitions; growth is expected from continued industrial-market recovery and positive organic growth across all verticals.
Reflects the sales-growth and margin assumptions above; the reconciliation table itemizes the mainly-amortization adjustments needed to reach the adjusted EPS range.
Same FY2027 outlook adjusted for expected intangible amortization (~$4.54/share), business realignment (~$0.74/share), and integration costs (~$0.19/share), net of tax effects.

CEO Jenny Parmentier framed FY2026 as a record year on all financial metrics and forecast FY2027 as another record year, citing broadening industrial recovery, organic growth across all verticals, and continued M&A integration (Curtis Instruments closed; Filtration Group and CIRCOR's aerospace-defense business pending).
